questions.q: List three major themes from "lwjnkl dh >ksaiM+h" that can serve as the basis for a structured class discussion.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) Aging and loss of dignity, (2) Family responsibility vs. selfishness, (3) Symbolism of the stick as self-respect. A wrong answer that lists plot events (e.g., "the stick breaks, the son gets angry, the old man leaves") reveals the student confuses discussion themes with narrative summary. They need to understand that themes are abstract ideas explored through events, not the events themselves.

questions.q: Explain why the stick is a powerful symbol for discussion, using one specific example from the text to support your explanation.
questions.a: Correct answer: The stick represents the old man's identity, history, and autonomy — it holds memories of his wife, his labor, and his independence. For example, when he says, "मेरे पास पाँच लकड़ियाँ हैं... ये मेरे जीवन की कमाई हैं" (I have five sticks... these are my life's earnings), it shows the stick is not a mere object but an extension of his self. A wrong answer that only says "it helps him walk" misses the symbolic layer and shows the student cannot move from literal to figurative interpretation.

questions.q: Given the discussion prompt "Is the son justified in his behavior toward his father?", outline two arguments for and two against, using textual evidence for each.
questions.a: Correct answer: For: (1) Son provides food and shelter — "पेट भरने के लिए नौकरी करता हूँ" (I work to fill stomachs). (2) He tries to reason — "अब तो वंज-चकज लक, एक हो गए हैं" (Now old age and childhood have become one). Against: (1) He dismisses father's feelings — "लकड़ी को फेंक दो" (Throw the stick away). (2) He prioritizes social image — "लोग क्या कहेंगे?" (What will people say?). A wrong answer that gives only one side or uses vague references ("he is mean") shows inability to balance perspectives or anchor arguments in the text.

questions.q: Compare the daughter-in-law's treatment of the old man with the grandson's attitude. What does this contrast reveal about generational change in the family?
questions.a: Correct answer: The daughter-in-law is cruel and calculating — she suggests breaking the stick ("लकड़ी को फाड़ दो") and measures worth in utility. The grandson, though initially silent, ultimately shows empathy — he picks up the stick and walks with the grandfather. This contrast reveals that while the middle generation internalizes transactional values, the younger generation still retains innate compassion, offering hope for restoration of dignity. A wrong answer that says "both are bad" or "grandson is good" without textual contrast shows superficial character reading.

questions.q: Judge the effectiveness of the ending (old man walking away with the stick) as a discussion starter. Does it resolve or deepen the conflict? Justify your evaluation.
questions.a: Correct answer: It deepens the conflict — the physical departure resolves the immediate cohabitation but opens moral questions: Can dignity survive without shelter? Is the stick enough? The open ending ("लकड़ी को कंधे पर रखकर... चल पड़ा") forces discussants to project consequences, making it highly effective for sustained debate. A wrong answer claiming "it resolves everything because he left" shows discomfort with ambiguity and a desire for narrative closure over thematic exploration.

questions.q: Design a 3-minute group discussion activity for classmates on "The stick as a metaphor for self-respect". Include an opening question, two follow-up questions, and a closing reflection prompt.
questions.a: Expected answer: Opening: "If the stick is the old man's self-respect, why does the family want him to discard it?" Follow-up 1: "When the son says 'throw it away', is he rejecting the object or the father's past?" Follow-up 2: "The grandson picks up the stick — what does this gesture say about inheriting dignity?" Closing: "Write one sentence: What 'stick' do you carry that defines your self-respect?" A poor activity would ask only recall questions ("How many sticks?") or lack progression from text to self, indicating the student doesn't understand discussion design as a scaffolded thinking process.
